title: Statistics in service of better, fairer health outcomes.
text:
PhD Student in Biostatistics · University of Nebraska Medical Center
    Statistics in service of better, fairer health outcomes.
    I'm a research statistician with seven years of experience in biomedical research, clinical data analysis, and health disparities research. My doctoral work focuses on clinical trial methodology, Bayesian statistics, causal inference, and the integration of machine learning into biostatistical practice.

  01About
  
    I work at the intersection of rigorous statistical methodology and applied biomedical research — designing analyses that hold up to scrutiny and translate into evidence that clinicians, investigators, and communities can use.
    Before beginning my PhD in Biostatistics at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, I worked at the University of Texas at El Paso's Border Biomedical Research Center, supporting studies in cardiometabolic disease, inflammatory aging, cancer, and health disparities. I have contributed to federally funded projects, including the All of Us Research Program.
    I'm both a research statistician and a data analytics professional. I use R and Python for statistical modeling — survival analysis, causal inference, general and generalized linear models, and linear mixed models — and SQL, Tableau and CRM data for descriptive and predictive analytics with higher-education and research data.
